rationale: Generic 'not elsewhere classified/not otherwise specified' CNS embryonal category with no defined anatomic restriction; occurs across the CNS sites in its ceiling.
Generic NOS descriptor for CNS embryonal tumors with no anatomic restriction to a subset of ceiling sites.
Central primitive neuroectodermal tumor acronym; a generic CNS embryonal category not restricted to a proper subset of its ceiling.
Generic CNS embryonal descriptor arising throughout the CNS; not confined to a proper subset of ceiling sites.

term: Central primitive neuroectodermal tumor / CNS embryonal tumor
rationale: Combined generic CNS embryonal label with no established restriction to a subset of ceiling sites.
NOS primitive neuroectodermal tumor; generic multi-site CNS embryonal descriptor, not anatomically restricted.
Generic NOS descriptor with no defined anatomic restriction within the ceiling.

Although 'supratentorial' implies location above the tentorium, this legacy term spans cerebrum/lobes/ventricles which represent the bulk of the ceiling; no fetched source establishes a clean proper-subset restriction expressible in the ceiling C-codes.

Medulloblastoma is a posterior-fossa/cerebellar tumor extending to brainstem and 4th ventricle; the code's ceiling (cerebellum, brain stem, brain NOS, overlapping) already reflects its natural home, so the term is not restricted to a proper subset of it.
A medulloblastoma histologic variant; occurs across the same cerebellum/brainstem/brain-NOS/overlapping ceiling and is not confined to a proper subset.
Molecularly defined medulloblastoma; arises in the cerebellum/midline with 4th-ventricle and brainstem involvement, covering essentially all of its ventricle/cerebellum/brainstem ceiling codes.
WNT-activated medulloblastoma subtype spanning the cerebellum/midline; not restricted to a proper subset of its CNS ceiling.
Classic-histology WNT medulloblastoma; occurs across cerebellum, ventricle and brainstem sites of the ceiling.
Large-cell WNT medulloblastoma variant; posterior-fossa tumor covering essentially all ceiling sites, no proper-subset restriction.

SHH medulloblastoma arises predominantly in the cerebellar hemispheres but also the vermis and extends to brainstem; the ceiling (cerebellum, brain stem, brain NOS) is already its home range, not a proper subset.
Non-WNT/non-SHH group-3 medulloblastoma; midline cerebellar/4th-ventricle tumor spanning the cerebellum, ventricle, brainstem and brain-NOS ceiling codes.
Group-4 medulloblastoma; midline posterior-fossa tumor covering essentially all of its CNS ceiling sites.
Molecular umbrella for group-3/4 medulloblastoma; posterior-fossa/cerebellar tumor, not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.

term: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes with C19MC-alteration
rationale: ETMR can arise anywhere in the CNS: ~70% supratentorial cerebral hemispheres, ~30% brainstem/cerebellum, and rarely the spine, covering essentially all C710-C721 ceiling sites.

term: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, C19MC-altered
rationale: Same entity as above; distributed across supratentorial hemispheres, brainstem, cerebellum and rarely spine, so it is not confined to a proper subset of the ceiling.

term: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, DICER1-mutated
rationale: Molecular ETMR subtype; shares the same broad CNS distribution (supratentorial, brainstem, cerebellum, spine) as other ETMR, no proper-subset restriction.

term: Embryonal tumor with multilayered rosettes, NOS
rationale: NOS ETMR without confirmed C19MC alteration; occurs throughout the CNS just as C19MC-altered ETMR, not anatomically restricted.

Generic mature ganglion-cell tumor of autonomic/peripheral nerve origin; within the code's CNS ceiling (brain stem, spinal cord, cauda equina, NS NOS) no source establishes restriction to a proper subset.

Choroidal ganglioneuroma is an ocular (choroid, C69) lesion, a site not represented among this code's ceiling codes (C717, C720, C721, C729); the anatomic restriction therefore cannot be expressed as a subset of the ceiling.
Descriptive synonym for ganglioneuroma; no evidence of restriction to a proper subset of the CNS ceiling codes.
Maturation-stage descriptor of ganglioneuroma; not anatomically restricted within the ceiling.
Gangliocytoma can manifest anywhere within the central nervous system, so it is not confined to a proper subset of the ceiling sites.
source_name: PMC7451506 Gangliocytomas of the Sellar Region review

rationale: This is a sellar-region (pituitary fossa, C751) tumor, but the sella/pituitary is not among this code's ceiling codes; the anatomic restriction cannot be expressed as a subset of the ceiling.
source_name: PMID 30109498 Mixed gangliocytoma-pituitary adenoma in the sellar region

rationale: Ganglioglioma most often occurs in the temporal lobe but can occur anywhere in the brain or spinal cord, spanning essentially the full CNS ceiling; no clean proper-subset restriction.
Synonym listed under the ganglioglioma code; no evidence of restriction to a proper subset of the CNS ceiling.
Synonym under the ganglioglioma code; generic mixed neuronal-glial descriptor without an established anatomic restriction.

Ganglioglioma (and its anaplastic form) is a central nervous system glioneuronal tumor of the brain and spinal cord; it does not arise in the non-CNS sites included in this code's ceiling (peritoneum C481/C482, adrenal C740/C741/C749, parathyroid C750, pituitary C751, craniopharyngeal duct C752, carotid/aortic body C754/C755, other endocrine C758/C759), so it is restricted to the CNS proper subset of the ceiling.
source_name: Mayo Clinic Ganglioglioma (CNS tumor of brain/spinal cord)

rationale: Central neurocytoma is defined as an intraventricular tumor; the vast majority are located entirely within the ventricles (lateral ventricle around the foramen of Monro, with third-ventricle involvement), restricting it to the ventricle within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Radiopaedia Central neurocytoma (WHO grade 2 intraventricular tumor)

rationale: WHO defines cerebellar liponeurocytoma as a neurocytic tumor of the cerebellum; the vast majority arise in the cerebellum (most often the cerebellar hemispheres), restricting it to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
source_name: Radiopaedia Cerebellar liponeurocytoma (WHO grade 2 cerebellar tumor)

rationale: Extraventricular neurocytoma is defined by its location outside the ventricular system, arising within the brain parenchyma (most frequently the cerebral hemispheres, also the cerebellum); it thus occupies a proper subset of the ceiling that excludes the ventricle (C715).
source_name: AJNR (PMC7051427) Imaging Findings of Extraventricular Neurocytoma

rationale: A hypothalamic/sellar-region neurocytoma location is not cleanly represented among this code's ceiling codes (cerebrum lobes, ventricle, cerebellum), so a valid ceiling subset cannot be assigned.
'Lipomatous medulloblastoma' is a historical synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a cerebellar tumor; it is therefore restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
'Medullocytoma' is a historical synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a cerebellar tumor; restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
The sellar region is not represented among this code's ceiling codes (cerebrum lobes, ventricle, cerebellum), so the anatomic restriction cannot be expressed as a valid ceiling subset.
Generic NOS neurocytoma without specification of ventricular vs extraventricular location; not restricted to a proper subset of the ceiling.
'Neurolipocytoma' is a synonym for cerebellar liponeurocytoma, a tumor of the cerebellum; restricted to the cerebellum within this code's ceiling.
A sellar-region neurocytoma location is not represented among this code's ceiling codes, so no valid ceiling subset can be assigned.

AT/RT has been described in virtually all CNS locations: ~52% posterior fossa/cerebellum, ~39% supratentorial cerebral hemispheres, plus pineal, brainstem and spinal cord, covering essentially the full CNS ceiling.
source_name: Cancer Management and Research (PMC5033212) AT/RT review

rationale: Although the MYC molecular subgroup is predominantly supratentorial, AT/RT as an entity occurs throughout the CNS and the subgroup is a molecular rather than a fixed anatomic restriction; no clean proper-subset confinement of the ceiling is established.
source_name: Cancer Management and Research (PMC5033212) AT/RT review

rationale: The SHH molecular subgroup of AT/RT occurs in both supratentorial and infratentorial compartments in a balanced distribution, spanning essentially the full CNS ceiling; not restricted to a proper subset.
source_name: Cancer Management and Research (PMC5033212) AT/RT review
